scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

He's also really into my friends and thinks they're the coolest, always wanting to hang out with us. My friends, who don't have little siblings, think he's super cute and hype him up a lot. My brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no, go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up, and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now, I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing and exhausting. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age wasn't a big deal. So, was it right or wrong for me not to force him to go to bed? Let me think about this step by step. First, I need to consider the importance of sleep for a 7-year-old. From what I know, children that age typically need around 10-12 hours of sleep per night. If he stayed up until midnight instead of his usual bedtime, that's a significant loss of sleep. The next day, he was cranky and didn't want to get up, which aligns with what happens when kids don't get enough sleep. Next, I should think about the responsibility aspect. My mom left me in charge, trusting me to handle things. She allowed my friend over, but she also expected me to ensure my brother went to bed on time. By letting him stay up, I went against her instructions, which is part of why she got mad. On the other hand, I didn't want to have a big fight with my brother, which would have been stressful and exhausting for everyone involved. I also considered that 2 hours of missed sleep wasn't a huge deal, but in reality, for a child, that can have noticeable effects. I also need to think about teaching responsibility. If I let him stay up, he might not learn that staying up late has consequences. However, if I had forced him to go to bed, it would have been a tough situation, and he might not have understood why he had to go. Another angle is the impact on our relationship. If I had forced him to go to bed, he might have been upset with me, affecting our sibling bond. By letting him stay, I maintained a positive relationship, but at the cost of his sleep and my mom's trust. I also need to consider the bigger picture. As a 18-year-old, I'm supposed to be setting an example and helping him learn responsibility. By not enforcing the bedtime, I might be sending the message that rules can be broken, which isn't ideal. Additionally, I should think about the long-term effects. Consistent sleep patterns are important for a child's development. If this becomes a regular occurrence, it could lead to more significant issues down the line. In summary, while letting him stay up avoided an immediate conflict and kept the mood positive, it went against my responsibilities and had negative consequences the next day. It also affected my relationship with my mom and potentially set a bad precedent for my brother. So, considering all these factors, it seems like not forcing him to go to bed was the wrong decision. It went against the expectations set by my mom, had negative effects on my brother's behavior the next day, and could impact his understanding of responsibility and consequences.
